handoff.reason: RCT found GLA 600 mg/day significantly INCREASED serum PSA by 15% versus baseline (opposite direction to EPA and CoQ10 arms, which decreased PSA) -- a safety-relevant signal for men monitoring PSA.

Cochrane review notes a case report of risk (inflammation, thrombosis, immunosuppression) with EPO/GLA taken beyond one year, and a separate report of increased bleeding risk when combined with warfarin.

identity_notes: GLA's retrieval set includes a large cluster of ENTERAL critical-care immunonutrition formula studies (Oxepa-type EPA+GLA+antioxidant diets for ALI/ARDS, sepsis, trauma, head/neck surgery) that are tube-fed in ICU settings, not oral supplement use -- all rejected not_this_route, consistent with the route hard-rule. A second cluster is genetic/observational PUFA-biomarker studies (GWAS, Mendelian randomization, FADS1/FADS2 SNP meta-analyses, cross-sectional PUFA-status comparisons) that measure endogenous n-6 fatty acid levels rather than testing a GLA intervention, rejected not_intervention. A third recurring pattern is dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA), a distinct downstream elongase metabolite of GLA, tested as its own supplement in several records -- rejected different_substance, though DGLA appears as a measured biomarker within several kept GLA trials. GLA's genuine oral evidence base is concentrated in atopic dermatitis/eczema (mixed results across many small trials; Cochrane review 23633319 and meta-analysis 15099370 both conclude no clinically relevant benefit), rheumatoid arthritis (a more consistent positive signal, especially at doses >=1400 mg/day per Cochrane reviews 19941324/21328257), diabetic peripheral neuropathy (consistently positive: 2159860, 8380765, and noninferior to alpha-lipoic acid in 31701699 and network meta-analysis 38295879), and dry-eye/ocular-surface indications (usually combined with linoleic acid). A very large share of kept records deliver GLA via evening primrose oil or borage seed oil (whole-plant-oil sources, appropriate to how GLA is typically supplemented) or combined with other omega-3/omega-6 fatty acids and antioxidants in proprietary multi-ingredient formulas (Neuroaspis PLP10, CEAG, various dry-eye/ADHD blends) -- these are flagged related_form_differs since GLA's own contribution cannot be isolated. Two notable safety-relevant findings are routed to handoff: GLA significantly increased serum PSA in healthy men (23199523), and EPO/GLA taken beyond one year carries a case-report safety signal per the Cochrane eczema review (23633319).
